item.title: Re: Missing Overseer Replacements?
item.content:encoded:
There was originally long list of all of the new Overseers, but… I just didn't like it. I'm pretty clearly not afraid to drop names for the sake of a good story but it was just a bunch of names, and I thought it hurt the end of the piece. Who the new Overseers are isn't important, and to suddenly introduce a bunch of new characters all at the same time with no intention of doing anything with them would've been a mistake.

Also, yes! I'm about to update it for 5k right now.

He was effectively talked out of it. Calvin was faced with the reality that not all of the foundation were archetypal evil boogeymen he thought they were at first - though some of them certainly were.

But the main reason is because even if he did destroy the Foundation, the being known as the Administrator would still exist. And would keep wreaking havoc upon their reality.

The Administrator exists because of the Foundation, and vice versa. The Foundation indexes and studies anomalies, and they are paradoxically created by the Administrator as a result, it’s just that it’s implied no one aside from O5-1 and their closest associates will ever know that.

item.title: Re: Eh

I don't DISLIKE the concept, hell I feel the opposite and the Broken God is one of my favourite 001 ever.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I have no words to describe just how much I like-no, love-this 001 proposal.
Not to rip off Mazed's comment, but holy shit do I like the lengths that these proposals go to.
The tying in of plenty of your other works as well as fueling where the kaktusverse is going next. The sheer 'anime' of the whole situation is another thing I really like about it, the willingness to go all out with the inclusion of things like 610, 682, Samsara, Malidramagiuan, that whole bit with Blackbird combining a serious fight with ridiculous happenings, so on and so on and so on.
Also, for everyone else, I just want to explain why I think the overseers aren't 'stupid'.
Thirteen; No time to prepare, had no idea what he was in for.
Twelve; Believed that his ability to see patterns would save him, and it nearly did.
Eleven; Just wanted to get the journal so they could have their name back.
Ten; She could turn into a giant snake-god-thing, of course she feels invincible. Wouldn't you?
Nine; Had basically had enough of the Foundation, so would rather die anyway than continue.
Eight; He just fucking died.
Seven; She was really only there to get the spear, start a civil war, and leave. She didn't expect that that would be her undoing, because she seems like one of those people who think that they're gods.
Six; He thought bringing 682 and 10k army troops would work. It most definitely would have if he hadn't been lured to that 610 village.
Five; He just wanted to show them a way out, he wanted to be nicer-er. So when they said 'nah man, fuck you', he decided that he'd rather leave them there, thus starting a fight. He got cocky because he didn't think anyone could kill all of his selves but he failed to account for Mr. Desmet. Would you?
Four; He just wanted to live and underestimated the Foundation's resolve.
Three; He wanted to execute the insurgents as payback for killing all his friends, but he underestimated them just like those before him.
Two; She had basically had enough of Aaron's shenanigans, so she peaced out of life.
One; Well, he brought a sword to a spear fight and died.
Administrator; Sometimes I wonder if he gave Calvin plot armour so he could have a change of scenery with who was in charge of the foundation?
I continue to stand by the idea that these people aren't idiots, they just underestimate their foes and put too much stock in their own abilities.
Also, I made the mistake of listening to The Way it Ends by Landon Pigg while reading the epilogue.
Tears. Mainly because I was fascinated by the music similarities to the events.

+1 for fucking sure.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Oh lord, this was fun.

The entire vibe is like, if Quentin Tarantino and Guillermo del Toro did a movie together. With a dash of Yoko Taro-flavored turbotragedy.

Without a shred of irony, I think the best parts were the ones that in other cases might seem like pandering or going over-the-top, like 682 vs. 610, the Samsara business, and the climax being a straight-up duel. It earns the spectacle by staying so consistent and paying dues to a gratifyingly enormous swathe of existing SCP writings and lore. This is a world where ridiculous things happen and this story demonstrates it with precision-guided enthusiasm.

The "you break it, you bought it" styled ending was, in my opinion, very easy to see coming, but it worked, and the good times here are not entirely, ironically, about how it ends.

item.title: Eh
item.content:encoded:
[WARNING: HEAVY SPOILERS]

This started out really strong but I really don't like how stupid the Overseers are in this. They have a ton of chances to kill the main characters and they don't use any of them. Besides, they know the main characters are coming, they know they're killing them in order, and in no moment they decide to counter-attack or at least make a plan to face them together, which would make it impossible for the heroes to win. This is extremely plot-convenient, especially because it's Calvin himself who chooses to face them in order instead of being purposefully unpredictable.

I really really like the idea of the cycle, but all the anime fights I had to read through to get to the twist really made me want to stop at times. Some of them are really interesting, but the majority of them are very overdramatic and exaggerated, including the one against 01 at the end (who is also kind of dumb, why didn't he just tell Calvin what was going on so he didn't have to die?). Like I said, the Broken God, the psychic children and the Dr Manhattan black hole are all awesome and well-developed ideas, but the serialized part at the end goes downhill very quickly.

Also the theme hurts my eyes.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
was this supposed to be a love letter to the Highlights Reel of famous Golden Age SCPs?

It was not. This was supposed to be the culmination of a story I started thinking about when I wrote my first 001 proposal, with elements included from everything I'd written or enjoyed reading about since then.

it is, in my opinion, not a very good one.

Can't win em all.

You have in this story a cowboy Overseer riding 682 using a whip to fight kaiju-sized Flesh That Hates.

I'm not going to go through this whole wall of text and address it point by point, but this is a pretty good example. This is one of those moments that if you can't enjoy it, you won't enjoy this proposal. I never intended it to be as nuanced as Past and Future, or as tight as A Record. It is what it is, because it is what I wanted it to be.

That's about it.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I may be missing the point dramatically here, and I sincerely apologize if I am, but was this supposed to be a love letter to the Highlights Reel of famous Golden Age SCPs?

If so, it is, in my opinion, not a very good one.

For one, it overindulges in itself. You have in this story a cowboy Overseer riding 682 using a whip to fight kaiju-sized Flesh That Hates. This was a tad too blatant for my tastes, and is the most egregious example in the work.

+ show block
– hide block

The mentions of various famous SCPs felt slightly forced- 173, for example, or THE DEER. Clef is not often as cordial and genuine as his journal would indicate. And some famous faces don’t show up at all, or are neglected- 106 makes no appearance. I didn’t see mentions of Herman Fuller. The Scarlet King is vaguely grazed over, I can’t remember mentions of Kain or Able.

The thing 001 is turns out to be somewhat simple, with little foreshadowing I could place (other than remarks about phones ringing) and vaguely defined. This may be the intent, as the entity would seem to literally be the embodiment of that which is undefined- but it was still a bit of a letdown for me personally.

The ending is strange. 001 seemed to rather easily convince Calvin to rebuild the Foundation. I don’t understand what happened to Olivia or what it is now.

Adam’s crush on Calvin had no foreshadowing I could detect (I may be an idiot).

The Kid, in my opinion, leaned too hard into the “eerie wrongness” state. It makes more sense in the context of the story, but the uncanny-valley-ness of O5-3’s appearance, speech, and “personality” seemed excessive. Its death, as well as being a rather clear attempt to symbolize how far Calvin has fallen, was also played for a bit too much grossout drama (even after its organs were pulpified it kept laughing for several seconds?)

I also don’t understand how your previous proposals are components of 001’s Ouroboros. They are vaguely mentioned or quickly brought in within the story itself, and the themes of the last three proposals don’t seem to reiterate themselves by the end of the story.

Also, when did Jesus turn into a lady? Or were they a lady all along? And why are they no longer a sinless paragon?

I apologize for rambling, and I apologize for probably being completely incorrect in my analyses. I adore the concept and writing, and I hope to see more of your work in the future, as long as it doesn’t have some of the (personally perceived) flaws this one does.

PS- Is the Serpent dead? Is 001 somehow related to the Serpent?

PPS- In one scene, where Calvin is running from 682 to get the Spear of the Non-Believer away from the American, it occurred to me that since the Spear kills gods, it might have been able to kill 682. And therefore, you, djkaktus, had an opportunity to kill 682, and it would have been literally the only scenario where this would have been acceptable in-universe and out, and you did not take it. I almost died laughing when this hit me.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts and properly space your paragraphs. ~Zyn

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Was the Chaos Insurgency, as was originally conceived, more in line with modern anti-fascist movements? The impression I'm getting is that Siegel's grand designs were either perverted or disregarded by a thorn-in-the-side philosophy, wherein the Foundation ought not to be destroyed, but countered. This seems to have resulted in excessive militarism within the CI that rivals the Foundation, as well as the coalescing of power into the hands of Delta Command.

Like, it's obvious through how members of the Insurgency talk that they see themselves as anti-fascist, to the extent that they hate the Foundation for doing evil things and the Foundation is also pretty fascist. But the modern Insurgency still carries a lot of similarities to the Foundation, from their rigid hierarchy to the "inner circle" dynamic of Delta to their emphasis on combat. Did Seigel originally envision a more decentralized union of individuals who would act autonomously, or was the idea always to have a Delta Command and a downward flow of orders to low-ranking members?

You might have stated the answer to this in one of your articles, but I originally read a lot of them when I didn't care as much about politics and hierarchy. Planning on revisiting them sometime soon. Feel free to direct me to an article if that's more convenient than explaining CI philosophy to me.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The short answer is yes - the CI undoubtedly see themselves, at least at some levels, as a counter to the fascist SCP Foundation.

The core conceit of these two organizations comes down, at least in this universe, to a fundamental question - is the torture of innocents worth staving off possible annihilation? The Foundation has answered that question, even as early as 231, with a pretty resounding "yes". The argument at the end of The Children is one of whether or not the ends justified the means. The Insurgency, led at that point by Aaron Siegel and Vince Arians, rejected that notion. They (at least Arians, anyway) saw what they had done to those kids and determined that no system that permits such evil is worth preserving.

In other words - if the endurance of the Earth requires terrible evil to be committed, then the Earth is not worth preserving.

item.title: A non-comprehensive list of references
item.content:encoded:
This is my attempt to document as many of the references made in this proposal as possible. I am only listing an article once (even if it appears multiple times) and I’m excluding the other Ouroboros articles.

On the Summa Modus Operandi hub:

  • SCP-2000
  • SCP-076 and other members of Omega-7
  • SCP-1730
+ Spoilers
- Close

In the journal:

  • Tanhony’s Proposal (similar in concept)
  • SCP-3000 (mention of the Bay of Bengal, the objects location)
  • The tale The Flytrap
  • SCP-093

In the logs:

  • SCP-006
  • SCP-610
  • SCP-3740 (first mention of the Spear of the Non-believer that I know of)
  • SCP-682
  • SCP-140 (multiple mentions of the Daevites)
  • SCP-1000 and SCP-4000
  • Clef’s 001 Proposal.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Excellent. I read through the whole thing without skimming, and unless there are hidden offsets I got it all. That would mean a +1…

normally. But I can't here. There are very few things I downvote on, and even then I try and mitigate them but the ones that feature prominently here are:

+ show block
– hide block
  1. Overseers are made of stupid. Maybe you're saying that the overseers are incapable of thought or free will, doing exactly the things that would get them killed. I can't imagine a universe in which Green would not have simply executed them. The claim is 'well, she's super evil'. Even if I let that slide, O5-6 does almost the exact same thing, like, less than 24 hrs later?
  2. If O5-1 was indeed so determined to stop Calvin, why is he chillin like Thanos?
  3. Appropriation (or rather, misappropriation) of religions iconography. Since its so ubiquitous I often try to let this slide, as I'd be throwing downvotes at just about everything. But you've got the stigmata here for no apparent reason, comparing Dr. Light to Christ themself, and the Lancea Longini starring as a primary mcguffin. Respect for religion aside, these have been tropes for literally a millennia. You can use this and still get a pass, but telekill is right out?

I mean, it is well written, I cannot deny that. It's just that I find some of the ingredients unpalatable.
-1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

Goddamn, O5-5's chapter ripped me up inside. That and the beautifully executed Chekov's gun that is the second vial of Fountain of Youth water. You know he has it before the other characters do, but by the time the gun goes off it's very possible to have forgotten about it. Vincethony is exactly the right person to warn him about using it on anyone, another great piece of symmetry in the Aaron/Vince = Calvin/Adam parallel. The "You should not have saved me" element which comes into play with Sophia AND Adam AND Olivia is a great underscoring of Aaron and Calvin both meaning to do good but producing only, well, chaos.

Aside from a few minor quibbles - CI having enough assets available in exactly the right places to rescue the crew despite being spread thin, The Children and The Broken God feeling a bit hollow as setup for the cycle - I think I have a new favorite novel.

item.title: Great, but let me nitpick
item.content:encoded:
I really liked the whole sequence that makes up Ouroborous, with only a few minor issues:
- there's some stuff a few combs through looking at grammar/spelling/syntax would clear up.
- the over reliance on deus ex machina, which I think other people have pointed out
- weird adjectives used occasionally, but that might just be me

I'm really only nitpicking that stuff because overall this is a solid SCP-001, it's generally very well-written and brings a lot of different SCPs together in an original way.
